newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields end steeply lower after RBNZ comment.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields end steeply lower after RBNZ comment.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
10-YR BONDS (DEC) 92.85 (UNTRADED) 10-YR 7.32 (-14)
OVERNIGHT CASH 10.85 PCT (PREV 9.85) US 30-YR 6.83 (PREV 6.85)
* RBNZ comments sends currency, yields spiralling
* Dealers suggest debt reaction relatively mild
* Local market awaiting foreign investors reaction
New Zealand yields were sent spiralling lower on Thursday by a late morning statement by the Reserve Bank saying that monetary conditions were tighter than necessary.
"What the Reserve Bank has done is faced reality. It's a reality check," said a Wellington bank dealer.
"I'm surprised it was only 30 points. The market got the green light...there is scope for rates to go lower," he said.
The RB's comment sent the New Zealand dollar down nearly one U.S. cent and the Trade-Weighted Index down to 66.79 from 67.54 at Wednesday's close.
But the RB's decision to fail an open market operation on commercial grounds shortly before its comment may have inhibited some players.

Cash zoomed up to 13.50 percent at one stage and finished nearly a point higher at 10.85 percent. Dealers said the system will be $80-$120 million short on Friday morning and some banks may be scrambling for discountable bills.
Another dealer said that the fact that the RB comment came from financial markets manager David Archer and not Governor Don Brash may have tempered the reaction.

"Reading between the lines, the bank is saying, 'We are comfortable but we are still in breach of the target so bear that in mind folks -- we'll let it go but we won't let it run away'," the dealer said.
There had already been offshore buying in the the 10 year and six year bonds before the RB's statement and afterwards there was panic buying across the curve on hefty volume.
The 10-year bonds ended 14 points lower at 7.32 percent but a couple of points off their session lows.
Dealers said the market will watch with interest to see if foreign holders take the RB's comment as a signal to take profits.
One dealer said there was activity in the swaps market which indicated there were still more euro and samurai issues the wind which would put fresh upward pressure on the currency.
-- Simon Louisson 64 4 4714 276
